title: Cavtat Mobile Network Coverage & Connectivity 2026
metaDescription: Navigating Cavtat? Get sharp, direct advice on mobile network coverage, eSIMs, and WiFi for 2026. Stay connected without hassle. Essential connectivity guide.
content:
## Mobile Network Quality
Cavtat's mobile coverage is strong. Main providers—A1, T-Hrvatski Telekom, Telemach—all deliver reliable 4G/LTE. Expect solid performance in town, along the coast, and on major routes. 5G is expanding, primarily in the central areas.

## Local SIMs & eSIMs
For non-EU visitors, a local prepaid SIM is the best value. This is usually not worth the extra cost of relying on daily international roaming packages. Pick one up at kiosks or provider stores in Dubrovnik airport. eSIMs are equally viable; services like Airalo or Holafly connect instantly.

## Wi-Fi Availability
Free Wi-Fi is prevalent in most hotels, apartments, cafes, and restaurants. Connection speeds vary. Public Wi-Fi is common but use with caution. This sounds convenient, but in practice it often causes problems with security and reliability. A VPN is recommended for sensitive tasks.

## Roaming for EU Visitors
EU/EEA citizens benefit from "Roam Like At Home" regulations. Your home plan's data, calls, and texts usually work at no extra charge. Check your provider's fair use policy.

## Connectivity Essentials
*   Major providers: A1, T-Hrvatski Telekom, Telemach. All offer good 4G/LTE and growing 5G.
*   eSIMs work reliably through global or regional providers.
*   Public Wi-Fi is widespread but often unsecured. Use a VPN.
*   Download offline maps and content for excursions outside primary coverage areas.
*   A local prepaid SIM offers the most data for your money if you're outside the EU/EEA.

faq.question: Is 5G available in Cavtat?
faq.answer: Yes, 5G is available in Cavtat's main areas and coastal promenade, primarily via A1 and T-Hrvatski Telekom, but coverage isn't universal yet.

faq.question: Can I rely on public Wi-Fi in Cavtat?
faq.answer: Public Wi-Fi is widespread but variable in speed and security. It's fine for light browsing, but a VPN is advised for sensitive activities.

faq.question: What's the best way to get data for a short trip?
faq.answer: For short trips, an eSIM from a global provider or a prepaid local SIM card from A1, T-Hrvatski Telekom, or Telemach offers the best data value and convenience.

Expect reliable 4G/LTE, with 5G expanding in urbanized zones and tourist hotspots. Roaming is generally seamless for EU citizens. Non-EU visitors should consider local SIMs or eSIMs for optimal value.
